passages.original: Ad convivium nuptiale nullus accedat : ne per lasciviam saecularium quae sunt saeculi reco- gnoscat; et, quod absit, ad mundi hujus vitam, etsi non corpore, animo revocetur, sicut dixit beatissimus Cyprianus : Adulterium dum videtur, et discitur (Ephes. ii). Qui joculare aliquid vel risui aptum in conventu fratrum proferre praesumpserit, vel qui cum junioribus verba otiosa narrare voluerit, aut habere amicitias aetatis infirmae, increpationi, ut dignus est, subjacebit.
passages.english: Let no one go to a wedding feast, lest through the wantonness of people of the world he come to recognize again the things that belong to the world, and, God forbid, be called back to the life of this world, if not in body, then in mind, as the most blessed Cyprian said: "Adultery, while it is watched, is also learned" (Eph. 2). Whoever presumes to bring out anything jesting or fit for laughter in the assembly of the brothers, or whoever chooses to tell idle tales with the younger ones, or to have friendships with those of a weak age, shall be subject to rebuke, as he deserves.
passages.notes: "reco- gnoscat" is read as "recognoscat" (a word split at a line-break). The quotation from Cyprian ("Adulterium dum videtur, et discitur") is compressed in the text; the sense taken is that adultery is learned while it is watched. The reference "Ephes. ii" printed after it does not fit a Cyprian quotation and may be an editorial error. "Aetatis infirmae" ("of a weak age") most likely means boys or the young.
